item.title: I’m a godfather, but I don’t impose appointments on governors — Osoba
item.description: By Efe Onodjae Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba has defended the role of political godfathers in Nigeria’s democracy, saying their responsibility should be to offer advice and guidance rather than impose political appointees on elected governors. Osoba, who spoke during a podcast hosted by Reuben Abati and shared on X (formerly Twitter), said he considered himself a political godfather but had deliberately avoided interfering in the administration of his political successors. According to him, he had never nominated anyone for appointment as commissioner, special adviser, councillor or local government chairman in the state. He said: “I agree, I’m a godfather. But one thing that is working for me in my state is that I hardly interfere. I counsel and advise him. I have never nominated one person into his government.” Explaining his position, the former governor said imposing candidates on an administration could undermine the governor’s authority and create unnecessary divisions among his political supporters. He noted that appointing one person from the numerous people around him could offend others, while anyone recommended by him might be viewed with suspicion within the administration. Osoba recalled that during his tenure as governor, he adopted a system that allowed each federal constituency to nominate candidates for commissioner positions. He said he requested one name from each federal constituency and subsequently reviewed their credentials before assigning them portfolios, adding that the approach helped him avoid pressure from political associates. The former governor maintained that political godfathers should ensure that people who worked for a candidate during electioneering campaigns were recognised and compensated, but should not dictate how an elected governor runs his administration. “That’s the role of a godfather. I agree, I’m a godfather,” he said. Osoba also defended the participation of experienced elders in candidate selection, citing his support for a presidential candidate whom he described as experienced, having served in the Lagos State House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate, as well as in the corporate sector. item.title: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for June 2028, suspect faces death penalty
item.description: The trial of the man accused of murdering US conservative firebrand Charlie Kirk will begin in June 2028, the judge said Monday. “Jury selection will begin June 21, 2028,” judge Tony Graf told the Utah district court, noting that 105 days have been reserved for the trial. Tyler Robinson, 23, faces a potential death penalty for allegedly killing Kirk with a gunshot to the neck on a university campus in the western US state of Utah on September 10, 2025. The killing of Kirk at age 31 at an event planned by his right-wing youth organization, Turning Point, sent shockwaves through the US political world. Kirk had become a popular leader in a Christian Nationalist movement that preaches traditional values while voicing intolerance for diversity and LGBTQ communities. Turning Point was key to mobilizing youth support for Donald Trump’s re-election as president in 2024. The group is now led by his wife, Erika Kirk. The prosecution had sought a trial as early as January 2028, while Robinson’s lawyers had wanted until the end of 2029 to prepare their defense. Last month, Trump criticized the judge and said the case “should be tried within a month, not three years.” Kirk’s assassination last year triggered a 33-hour manhunt culminating in Robinson surrendering to authorities. He has pled not guilty. The prosecution has presented text messages in which Robinson confessed to planning the murder to his roommate, a transgender person with whom they allege Robinson was in a relationship. The defense has focused on alleged weaknesses in the DNA and ballistic evidence. item.title: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi Will Collapse Under Their Own Weight — SDP’s Adewole
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Adewole Adebayo, has said he is confident of victory in a free, fair, and credible 2027 election. Adebayo said that other candidates like President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Atiku Abubakar of the Africa Democratic Party (ADC) and Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Party (NDC) will fall under their own weight. Speaking during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, he said that his manifesto, Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity, is a pathway to progress and good governance that can be deployed to improve the lives of Nigerians “They will collapse under their own weight; that is not the issue. What I want to defeat is poverty and insecurity. “But to defeat that, you need to defeat ignorance in people going to just vote based on sentiment or looking for something,” Adebayo said. “You also have to defeat lethargy where people get tired, ‘Oh, my vote doesn’t count. You also have to defeat apathy. “So, once we do that, we will defeat anybody. When we say defeat, it’s not a wrestling match; it’s about convincing the majority of your fellow citizens to believe in this plan. To say this plan is going to work.” Adebayo says his manifesto will improve the lives of Nigerians. According to him, fixing the government will fix the security challenges in the country. The SDP candidate said that Nigerians should not see terrorists anymore in six months, given the capacity of the Nigerian Armed Forces. Adewole promises to address banditry, saying that citizens will get security as a Christmas present in 2027. The presidential election is scheduled to be held on January 16, 2027. item.title: Governor Idris pardons, reinstate suspended Commissioner in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi Kebbi State Governor, Dr. Nasir Idris has directed the reinstatement of the Commissioner for Animal Health, Husbandry and Fisheries, Alhaji Kabir Usman Alaramma, to his position. The Honourable Commissioner for Information and Culture, Alhaji Yakubu Ahmed Birnin Kebbi, disclosed this shortly after the State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Nasir Idris at the Council Chamber of Government House, Birnin Kebbi. According to the Commissioner, the reinstatement of the suspended Commissioner is with immediate effect. With this directive, the Commissioner of Information stated, the suspension previously imposed on the Commissioner had formally been lifted. “Consequently, he has been reinstated to his position and is hereby directed to resume his official duties with immediate effect,” the Commissioner said. The reinstatement underscores the commitment of the Kebbi State Government to effective governance, administrative responsibility, and the continued strengthening of party and stakeholder engagement across the state. item.title: 2027: ‘Tinubu Is Fit To Go,’ APC National Chairman Dismisses Claims Challenging President’s Health — Nentawe Yilwatda
item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s health ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the President is fit to contest. The APC chairman stated this on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. ﻿ He urged Nigerians not to interpret isolated expressions of dissent against the President as evidence of widespread unpopularity. Addressing concerns about Tinubu’s limited attendance at some presidential campaign rallies, Yilwatda said the President could not be expected to participate in every campaign activity while discharging his constitutional responsibilities. He said some public officials had been advised to attend selected rallies rather than all the engagements to prevent governance from suffering. Following Tinubu’s earlier announcement that he would not attend every campaign rally because of the responsibilities of his office, the APC chairman said the President’s absence should not be interpreted as a sign of weakness or inability to lead the party’s re-election effort. Muslim-Muslim Ticket Yilwatda also defended the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket of Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima, dismissing concerns that the arrangement would marginalise Christians under the APC administration. He maintained that Christians had continued to have their voices heard in government, adding that those the party had engaged were comfortable with the arrangement. “Most Christians that we’ve engaged and we’ve spoken to them, they are very okay with the Muslim-Muslim ticket,” he said. “The thought and the fear of most Christians was that the Muslim-Muslim ticket may suppress their voices, but their voices are heard loud and clear now.” He also argued that Christians had not suffered molestation because of Tinubu’s religion during the President’s three years in office. ADC Crisis Reacting to the Federal High Court judgment invalidating the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the APC chairman denied that his party had any involvement in the opposition party’s internal crisis. He questioned why the ADC was blaming the ruling party over a legal dispute instituted by one of its members. Asked whether he was pleased that the ADC was facing a leadership crisis, Yilwatda said he was not bothered by the development. Yilwatda expressed confidence that Tinubu would defeat Atiku in a free and fair election. He argued that Atiku’s performance in the 2023 presidential election was largely attributable to the political structure of the PDP rather than his individual popularity. “He did not win because of Atiku; he won because of the structure of the PDP. It was the PDP that brought Atiku, not Atiku winning on his own,” he said. item.title: Full list: 2026/2027 FA Cup second round fixtures confirmed
item.description: Wimborne Town have been handed a home tie against Bradford City in the second round of the FA Cup, while Leicester City will travel to non-league side Dover Athletic. Seventh-tier Wimborne are among the lowest-ranked teams remaining in the competition after producing one of the biggest upsets of the first round by defeating League Two side Crawley Town. The Magpies will now welcome League One outfit Bradford City as they look to continue their impressive FA Cup run. Leicester, who won the competition in 2021, must overcome Dover Athletic away from home to book their place in the third round. Leyton Orient will host Port Vale, last season’s quarter-finalists, while 2013 FA Cup winners Wigan Athletic have been drawn against Barnsley in an all-League One encounter. Jack Wilshere’s Luton Town will travel to AFC Fylde, while the winner of the postponed Plymouth Parkway versus Berkhamsted tie will host Barnet. The second-round fixtures will be played across the weekend of December 5, 2026. item.title: Jensen Huang: 5 things to know about viral Nvidia CEO’s affair with Chinese executive
item.description: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, whose chips power the global AI boom and who has the ear of President Donald Trump, has admitted to an affair with a Chinese executive who US intelligence reportedly believes was working for Beijing. Here is what we know: – What happened? – Huang, 63, acknowledged the relationship Sunday in a message to Nvidia employees. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he wrote. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang has been married to his wife Lori since 1985. His admission followed reports in The New York Times that US intelligence officials had concluded the woman, Alice Huang, was passing information to China. She is not related to the Nvidia chief. Nvidia had previously said that his interactions with her were “not unusual or unexpected” given their business ties. – Who is Alice Huang? – Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a senior executive at Megaspeed. The Singapore-based data center company was spun off from a Chinese company in 2023, and it rents out computing power from Nvidia chips. The Wall Street Journal reported that she and Huang were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025. According to the Times, a memo circulated among senior US officials this spring cited intelligence that she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. The memo said she had been recruited to gather information on Huang and possibly to steer Nvidia toward pushing for its top chips to be sold in China. The Journal said that authorities in Singapore and Taiwan also suspected Chinese intelligence had recruited her after learning of her closeness to Huang. Her current whereabouts are unclear. US officials suspect Megaspeed of helping smuggle restricted chips into China and the Justice Department has taken over a federal investigation into the company. Megaspeed has previously described itself as a “compliant and legitimate company.” Beijing rejected the allegations. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Monday that “the narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing.” – Why does it matter? – Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the chips used to train and run AI models. Washington has restricted sales of the most advanced ones to China since 2022 under the Biden administration. Huang has also been one of Trump’s most influential informal advisers on AI. The Journal reported that intelligence officials suspected the affair while Huang was lobbying the White House to allow chip exports to China. Late last year, he pushed to sell Nvidia’s most powerful chips there, an effort that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and other officials blocked. Trump instead allowed sales of a less advanced chip, with the US government taking a 25 percent cut. item.title: Nvidia Shares Plunge As Board Probes CEO Over China Spy Reports
item.description: AI chip behemoth Nvidia was plunged into turmoil Monday after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having an affair, with reports saying US officials believe the woman was spying for China. Beijing denied the claim, but shares of the chipmaker tumbled after Nvidia’s board opened an inquiry into reports that Huang was “the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” Near 1610 GMT, Nvidia shares were down 5.5 percent after losing nearly nine percent earlier in the session. (FILES) The logo of Nvidia is seen during a production preview exhibition in Taipei on May 21, 2025. (Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP) Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials determined that Alice Huang, a Chinese executive linked to Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, had been funneling information to Beijing. This screengrab from video footage by CTI obtained via AFPTV on November 9, 2026 shows Alice Huang (2nd R in pink), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (2nd L in black, back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP The executive, also known as Huang Le and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang, developed a close relationship with him, the Times said. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” Huang said in a message to company employees. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Jensen Huang is a central figure in the AI boom and a close informal adviser to US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly opposed regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand. The Times said Alice Huang’s relationship with the Nvidia chief could have given her insights into Trump’s thinking around AI. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing Monday that “the narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing.” AI is likely to come up when Trump meets President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China. ‘You Never Know’ Asked Sunday whether Huang would join the president’s Asia trip, which includes the Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen, Trump told reporters: “I don’t know, but I’ll certainly take him.” Trump said Huang was “a fine person, but you never know what’s going on. I’m sure — I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job.” Nvidia’s board said in a statement Sunday it had opened an independent probe “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” “While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” it said. item.title: Manchester United are becoming a club of survival rather than ambition
item.description: The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa felt like a victory at Old Trafford, but the fact that supporters could celebrate a point while their club sits in the relegation zone tells a more troubling story about how far United’s expectations have fallen. There was a time when a draw at Old Trafford felt like a defeat. Manchester United were a club built around winning, where anything short of three points could leave supporters disappointed, regardless of the performance. The expectation was not simply to compete but to dominate, to set the standards and to make winning feel like an obligation. Those expectations seem increasingly distant. On Sunday, Manchester United celebrated a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa with the sort of emotion usually reserved for a significant victory. Two goals in stoppage time, courtesy of Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, rescued a point after Michael Carrick’s side had twice fallen two goals behind. The comeback was extraordinary, the atmosphere was electric and the players had every reason to appreciate their resilience. But perhaps the most revealing aspect of the afternoon was not the comeback itself. It was how much it meant. Manchester United are now in a position where avoiding defeat feels like an achievement. A point against Aston Villa, under ordinary circumstances, would hardly have been considered a successful afternoon for a club of United’s stature. Yet the circumstances have become so desperate that the draw felt like a victory. That is how quickly footballing standards can collapse. United sit 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 matches . They have managed just one league victory, recorded against Ipswich Town in August, and Sunday’s result extended their winless league run to eight matches. It is a club-record sequence in the Premier League. The numbers are alarming, but the deeper concern is what they reveal about the club’s changing relationship with success. Manchester United have become a team defined by what they are trying to avoid rather than what they are trying to achieve. Instead of discussing title challenges, European qualification or the development of a convincing footballing identity, the conversation increasingly revolves around managerial uncertainty, defensive mistakes, relegation calculations and the possibility of another disappointing weekend. Survival has become the immediate ambition. And that is a remarkable development for a club whose history was built on refusing to accept anything less than excellence. Sunday’s performance captured both sides of United’s current identity. There was the determination to fight back, the willingness to keep attacking and the refusal to surrender even when the game appeared beyond them. Coming back from 2-0 down, reaching 2-2, falling behind again and eventually recovering from 4-2 demonstrated a spirit that supporters have desperately wanted to see. item.title: 2027: INEC removes 1.6m names from voters register
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why those who registered in the third phase of its Continuous Voter Registration CVR are yet to have their Permanent Voter Cards even as it announced a massive purge of the national voter register ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing a press conference in Abuja, the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, disclosed that the commission has successfully removed 1,609,553 invalid and deceased records from the system. “The Commission recognises that the detection of irregularities raises legitimate questions about how they arose. The response is evidence-led investigation, completed corrective action and stronger preventive controls. “1,609,553 records have been removed, comprising 1,608,660 confirmed invalid registrations and 873 verified deceased-voter records. INEC will continue to communicate verifiable aggregate outcomes while protecting personal information and the integrity of ongoing investigations”, said Amupitan. Addressing reporters regarding the status of unprinted cards, the INEC Chairman stated: “The distribution of Phases 1 and 2 of the PVC and transferred PVCs is on-going at the various LGAs in Nigeria. Some of the PVC for the third and final Phase are being delivered and they would be dispatched to the States by next week. “Meanwhile as from 1st December 2026, distribution will go back to the Registration Areas all over Nigeria. We appeal to those that registered in the third pahse to be a little bit patient since the production is done outside the country”. Vanguard recalls that those who registered in total in the third phase were 2,970,257 before the commission’s de-duplication protocol. The sweeping clean-up of the register followed widespread public outcry and intense scrutiny over anomalies spotted on the preliminary register displayed between October 9 and 15, 2026. A rigorous technical audit utilizing the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) uncovered systemic manipulations, including unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs, and fraudulent multiple registrations. Crucially, the investigation indicted internal personnel who abused their offices. Prof. Amupitan revealed that the commission identified 54 staff members cutting across 10 states who deliberately bypassed standard operating procedures and exploited special provisions meant for vulnerable citizens, such as persons with disabilities. Disciplinary actions and possible prosecutions have been initiated against the culprits. Reacting to media inquiries surrounding court cases involving political actors, the INEC Chairman maintained that the electoral umpire operates strictly on authenticated legal instruments rather than speculative reports. “On ADC/Atiku: as of today, we have not received the Certified True Copy of the court judgment and we don’t act based on what we see on the social media”, he said. item.title: Public Notice To Gaming Operators And The General Public.
item.description: FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY LOTTERY REGULATORY OFFICE (FCT-LRO) O ﬃ ce of the Director-General PUBLIC NOTICE TO GAMING OPERATORS AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC. FCT-LRO COMMENCES FULL BUSINESS OPERATIONS The Federal Capital Territory Lottery Regulatory Oﬃce (FCT-LRO) hereby informs gaming operators, industry stakeholders and the general public that the Oﬃce has commenced operations as the regulatory authority responsible for the oversight, regulation and supervision of gaming activities within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). 1. REGULATORY JURISDICTION Following the Supreme Court judgment in Attorney-General of Lagos State & 21 Others v. Attorney-General of the Federation & 15 Others, Suit No. SC/1/2008, the constitutional position on the regulation of lotteries and gaming has been clarified. By virtue of Section 299 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), the FCT has a distinct constitutional status, with the National Assembly exercising legislative powers ordinarily vested in a State House of Assembly. Accordingly, gaming operators conducting business within the FCT are required to comply with the applicable FCT licensing and regulatory requirements and engage with the FCT- LRO on all regulatory matters. 2. ONLINE GAMING OPERATIONS The Oﬃce clarifies that the Supreme Court judgment did not expressly settle the full regulatory framework applicable to online gaming. In particular, the judgment did not establish that any one State has exclusive regulatory control over the online gaming market. Accordingly, the online gaming market remains open to operators and investors. Operators are free to choose the regulator from whom they wish to obtain their gaming licence or authorisation, based on their business model, operational needs and the regulatory framework they consider most suitable and beneficial to their business. This choice may be exercised without undue interference, intimidation or coercive treatment by any State regulator solely on the basis that an operator has elected to obtain its licence from another regulator, as every state is duly empowered to regulate gaming activities within its relevant jurisdiction. Operators are, however, reminded that the online nature of a gaming platform does not, in itself, exempt an operation from applicable licensing and regulatory obligations where such obligations arise. The FCT-LRO remains committed to providing a transparent, consistent and predictable regulatory environment for digital gaming operations within the Federal Capital Territory. 3. NOTICE TO FORMER NLRC LICENSEES All gaming operators previously licensed by the National Lottery Regulatory Commission (NLRC) who are currently operating, or intend to operate, within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) are hereby required to approach the FCT-LRO to regularise their regulatory status. item.title: 2027: NDC will provide all-inclusive government – Kwankwaso
item.description: By Henry Umoru Ahead of January 16 2027 election, the Vice Presidential Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has promised Nigerians that an NDC-led Federal Government under Peter Obi and himself will operate an all-inclusive government. According to him, the Obi-led government would prioritise the interests of every Nigerian, irrespective of political, ethnic, religious or social affiliations. The former Kano State Governor spoke while addressing party leaders, stakeholders and supporters during a carnival-like reception organised in his honour at Toru-Orua, the country home of Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, National Leader of the NDC and the party’s Senatorial candidate for Bayelsa West. In a statement signed by the Coordinator, Ofurumapepe Media of the NDC Campaign Council, Gabriel Ukuta, he explained that Kwankwaso said that what Nigeria needed at this moment in the nation’s political history is a government that would deliberately carry its citizens along in the formulation, implementation of policies and programmes. He said that governance must be people-oriented and responsive to the needs and aspirations of the population. Kwankwaso said the NDC has positioned itself as a credible alternative political platform with the capacity, leadership and commitment to deliver the inclusive governance Nigerians desire. The NDC Vice Presidential Candidate said, “Nigerians deserve a government that will listen to them, accommodate their interests and ensure that no section of the country is left behind. An NDC-led Federal Government will be an all-inclusive government that will carry everybody along in its policies and programmes,” Kwankwaso who condemned what he described as the prevailing hunger, economic hardship and insecurity under the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led Federal Government, urged Nigerians to take advantage of the 2027 general elections to vote out the ruling party. The Vice Presidential Candidate who called on citizens to take collective responsibility for the electoral process by coming out en masse to vote for the NDC and ensuring that their votes count, expressed concern over alleged attempts by anti-democracy forces and agents of the ruling party to manipulate the outcome of the forthcoming elections, insisting that Nigerians must remain vigilant and protect their votes. “Voting is not enough; Nigerians must also take responsibility for protecting their votes. We must all work together to ensure that the wishes of the people are respected and that the outcome of the elections reflects the collective decision of the electorate,” he added. He expressed appreciation to Senator Dickson, members of the NDC National Working Committee (NWC), the National Campaign Council (NCC), party stakeholders, candidates and supporters across Bayelsa State for the impressive reception accorded him. item.title: Republican launches impeachment against US defense chief
item.description: A Republican lawmaker moved Monday to impeach US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran, setting up a potentially explosive vote in Congress just days after President Donald Trump’s party suffered a crushing midterm defeat. Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment accusing Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief. item.title: UK man convicted of fraud for secretly working five government jobs at once
item.description: A 56-year-old civil servant in the United Kingdom, UK, Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of nine counts of fraud after secretly holding multiple full-time government jobs and fraudulently earning more than £284,000 in taxpayers’ money. Chowdhury, from east London, held five overlapping government positions in the spring of 2023, concealing his multiple employment arrangements from the departments that hired him. After seven hours of deliberation, a jury unanimously found him guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by failure to disclose. The prosecution accused Chowdhury of “deliberate, intentional dishonesty” and “exploiting the system” to secure multiple salaries from public sector employers. During the proceedings, the judge said Chowdhury faced a “very significant custodial sentence”. He also refused him bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and Chowdhury’s own wellbeing. Sarah Melo, a specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate, described his actions as sustained dishonesty. “This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty,” Melo said. “He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing.” A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Chowdhury had “abused the trust placed in him as a public servant”. The department added that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of his offending. Between 2020 and 2023, Chowdhury held eight overlapping full-time public sector positions and earned a total of £350,000, according to evidence presented in court. Prosecutors told the court that he provided inaccurate information about his employment status on job application forms and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already employed as a civil servant. After securing the positions, he also failed to inform his employers that he was working for other government departments. Chowdhury was permitted to work entirely from home after telling his employers he was caring for his mother, with whom he lived in east London. His mother had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. However, rather than reduce his workload to care for her, he continued taking on additional government positions. In the spring of 2023, he held positions across the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During the period, he was contracted to work 183 hours a week, exceeding the total number of hours available in seven days. item.title: Full list: Canada lists foreigners eligible for rural permanent residence
item.description: Canada has outlined six eligibility requirements for foreign nationals seeking permanent residence through its Rural Community Immigration Program, a pathway designed to attract skilled immigrants to participating rural communities across the country. The programme offers permanent residence to eligible foreigners who want to work and settle in selected Canadian communities, particularly areas seeking skilled migrants to fill positions that cannot be filled by local residents. According to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), participating communities will approve designated employers to recruit skilled foreign nationals for available positions. To qualify for permanent residence under the programme, applicants must obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community and secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within that community. They must also have at least one year, equivalent to 1,560 hours, of related work experience within the previous three years. Other requirements include demonstrating language proficiency through an approved test, possessing a Canadian educational credential or its foreign equivalent, and providing proof of sufficient funds to support themselves and their families. Full list of eligibility requirements According to IRCC, foreigners seeking permanent residence through the programme must meet the following six requirements: Community recommendation: Obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community in Canada. Valid job offer: Secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within the participating community. Work experience: Have at least one year (1,560 hours) of related work experience within the past three years. Language proficiency: Demonstrate English or French language ability by taking an approved language test. Educational qualification: Possess a Canadian educational credential or a foreign equivalent. Proof of funds: Provide evidence of having sufficient money to support themselves and their families after arriving in Canada. The programme is designed to help participating rural communities attract skilled foreign nationals while providing immigrants with an opportunity to obtain permanent residence and establish themselves in Canada. Applicants are required to satisfy the eligibility conditions and secure the necessary community recommendation and employment offer before applying for permanent residence. item.title: FG suspends broadcast licence fee reviews indefinitely
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has suspended all reviews of broadcast licence fees indefinitely following concerns by operators over rising operational costs and financial pressures facing Nigeria’s broadcasting industry. The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, announced the decision on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by a delegation of the Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria (BON), led by its Chairman, Senior High Chief Dr Tony Akiotu. The decision followed BON’s 82nd General Assembly in Calabar, Cross River State, where the organisation raised concerns about the sustainability of broadcast operations amid mounting economic challenges. In a statement issued on Monday night by the Minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Rabiu Ibrahim, Idris said the suspension was part of efforts by the Federal Government to create a more conducive operating environment for broadcasters. “Any increase in licence fees is hereby put on hold. All reviews relating to licences are suspended until further notice. I am directing the NBC to ensure strict compliance while we review the situation,” he said. The minister also directed the Director-General of the National Broadcasting Commission (NBC) to expedite the review of the National Broadcasting Code to ensure that its provisions reflect current developments and emerging realities in the industry. On the Digital Switch-Over (DSO) programme, Idris promised to convene a stakeholders’ meeting to address outstanding concerns and resolve challenges affecting its implementation. He further disclosed that he had directed the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON) to ensure full enforcement of the 45-day payment period for advertising services, following BON’s request for improved compliance with the policy. The minister also assured the delegation that the ministry would engage relevant stakeholders on concerns surrounding access to affordable financing and spectrum allocation. Describing broadcasting as critical to national development, Idris said the industry played an important role in strengthening democracy, promoting national cohesion and ensuring public access to credible and accurate information. With the 2027 general elections approaching, he urged broadcasters to uphold professionalism, fairness and ethical standards in their reportage. “Freedom of expression must go with responsibility. You cannot simply say anything and claim to be practising journalism. “Journalism has standards, procedures and ethics. I urge broadcasters to ensure that what they report is factual, responsible and promotes national unity and peaceful coexistence,” the minister said. Earlier, BON Chairman, Akiotu, commended Idris for his intervention during the June 2026 DSO launch, noting that the stakeholders’ meeting convened by the minister helped address concerns about ensuring a level playing field for operators. item.title: Turkey Steel Factory Explosion Kills 16, Injures 13
item.description: An explosion ripped through a steel plant in western Turkey on Monday, killing 16 people and injuring 13, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said, announcing investigations into the tragedy. Eight workers were trapped at the HABAS steel factory about 60 kilometres (37 miles) north of the port city of Izmir, where the blast struck around midday (0900 GMT), said Izmir governor Suleyman Elban. Footage posted online showed a huge cloud of thick smoke pouring into the sky as flames appeared to engulf a tall structure within the HABAS Demir Celik plant in Aliaga. “The circumstances surrounding this tragic incident, which has deeply saddened our nation, including how and why it happened, whether there was any negligence, and who bears responsibility, will be established,” Erdogan said on television. Turkey’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan talks with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung during their meeting at the presidential Blue House in Seoul on November 3, 2026. Photo by JEON HEON-KYUN / POOL / AFP He said two of the injured were in serious condition. HABAS is a privately owned group and one of Turkey’s top steel producers. Crane Collapse According to Izmir’s governor, the blast was caused by an overhead crane that collapsed into a large industrial furnace used during the liquid steel casting process. “While a boiler replacement operation was being carried out at the HABAS iron and steel factory, the overhead crane fell and landed in the arc furnace, causing an explosion in the steel mill behind it,” Elban told reporters, referring to a large electric-powered steelmaking furnace. An eyewitness, Deniz Ulker, said it felt like an “earthquake”. “When I looked at the factory across the street, thick black smoke was coming out. A fire broke out where the chimney was,” Ulker told Anadolu news agency. “It was like a bomb going off,” said Turan Ilbay, who works as a truck driver at the factory and also spoke to Anadolu. Izmir mayor Cemil Tugay said on X that rescue teams were “continuing their work to remove the collapsed platform” and that those affected were factory workers. Safety Issues Workers’ groups said there was a long record of safety issues at HABAS. Contacted by an AFP journalist, HABAS declined to answer questions. Before Monday’s explosion, the Evrensel daily said at least 11 workers had died over the past decade while working there. Turkey’s Labour Party, a small Marxist faction, said on X it was the third time in three weeks that workers had lost their lives at HABAS. item.title: 2027: Why we’re yet to print over 2.9m PVCs — INEC
item.description: ….Removes 1,609,553 multiple, deceased registrants ….Identifies 54 staff responsible for multiple registration, unusual registration patterns, substituted photos ….Yet to receive CTC of judgment on Atiku/ADC By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why those who registered in the third phase of its Continuous Voter Registration CVR are yet to have their Permanent Voter Cards even as it announced a massive purge of the national voter register ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing a press conference in Abuja, the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, disclosed that the commission has successfully removed 1,609,553 invalid and deceased records from the system. “The Commission recognises that the detection of irregularities raises legitimate questions about how they arose. The response is evidence-led investigation, completed corrective action and stronger preventive controls. “1,609,553 records have been removed, comprising 1,608,660 confirmed invalid registrations and 873 verified deceased-voter records. INEC will continue to communicate verifiable aggregate outcomes while protecting personal information and the integrity of ongoing investigations”, said Amupitan. Addressing reporters regarding the status of unprinted cards, the INEC Chairman stated: “The distribution of Phases 1 and 2 of the PVC and transferred PVCs is on-going at the various LGAs in Nigeria. Some of the PVC for the third and final Phase are being delivered and they would be dispatched to the States by next week. “Meanwhile as from 1st December 2026, distribution will go back to the Registration Areas all over Nigeria. We appeal to those that registered in the third phase to be a little bit patient since the production is done outside the country”. Vanguard recalls that those who registered in total in the third phase were 2,970,257 before the commission’s de-duplication protocol. The sweeping clean-up of the register followed widespread public outcry and intense scrutiny over anomalies spotted on the preliminary register displayed between October 9 and 15, 2026. A rigorous technical audit utilizing the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) uncovered systemic manipulations, including unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs, and fraudulent multiple registrations. Crucially, the investigation indicted internal personnel who abused their offices. Prof. Amupitan revealed that the commission identified 54 staff members cutting across 10 states who deliberately bypassed standard operating procedures and exploited special provisions meant for vulnerable citizens, such as persons with disabilities. Disciplinary actions and possible prosecutions have been initiated against the culprits. item.title: TenTrade brings financial market experts together to promote trading education in Lagos
item.description: Financial services company, TenTrade, has brought together financial market experts, traders and industry stakeholders in Lagos to discuss ways of expanding participation in financial markets and preparing the next generation of traders. The gathering, held in Ikeja on Saturday, November 7, 2026, was themed, “One Community, One Future: Building the Next Generation of Traders.” The event featured discussions on financial market education, trading opportunities and the future of the trading industry in Africa. Speaking at the event, Wilfred Obasi, Regional Director for Africa at TenTrade, identified impatience and the desire to make quick money as major challenges confronting young traders. “For young traders, they are not patient enough. People want to make quick money. It is why we are making the event work today to enlighten young traders,” Obasi said. He explained that the event was organised to expose young people to the realities of financial trading and help them develop the patience and knowledge required to navigate the market. Obasi also spoke about the company’s international expansion, noting that TenTrade had grown from operating in one or two regions to having a presence in about 30 countries, including Kenya, Ghana, Nigeria and Indonesia. He attributed the company’s growth to its emphasis on building trust and empowering clients. “We make sure that we do not overpromise. We empower our clients and we do well for them,” he said. Also speaking, Ademola Adeagbo, Head of Education at TenTrade Africa, urged traders to prioritise risk management, discipline and trading psychology to achieve consistency in the financial markets. He identified fear, greed, fear of missing out (FOMO) and revenge trading as common emotional traps that could undermine trading decisions and expose traders to losses. Adeagbo stressed that traders must develop the discipline to manage risks and avoid making decisions based on emotions. Similarly, Kehinde Shogeke, TenTrade’s Sales Team Lead, said traders needed adequate market knowledge, sufficient capital and discipline to improve their chances of navigating the financial markets. He observed that many people entered forex trading without understanding its fundamentals, viewing it instead as an opportunity to make quick money. “Most traders or new traders see forex as a get-rich-quickly scheme. There is a basic knowledge of the market that they must have. Have a good knowledge, capital and discipline,” he said. Shogeke further explained that TenTrade offered different account options to accommodate traders with varying needs, including regular brokerage and funded accounts. According to him, the company’s regular brokerage offering provides up to six types of accounts, while its equity account allows traders to access up to $500,000. item.title: Nasarawa APC protests alleged violence, SDP alleges bias
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Members and supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Nasarawa State on Monday staged a protest in Lafia over alleged political violence, intimidation of party members and the disruption of the party’s presidential rally attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Addressing journalists and security officials during the demonstration, the state APC Chairman, Dr. Aliyu Bello, called for investigations into reported attacks on party supporters, including the alleged killing of a supporter in the Tudun Wada area of Lafia. Bello expressed concern over what he described as the failure of law enforcement agencies to act on complaints previously submitted by the party. He said the protest was organised to demand justice and adequate protection for party members, insisting that the APC remained committed to peaceful political activities. “We came here to demand justice that a full-scale investigation be carried out and the perpetrators of these acts arrested and prosecuted,” he said. The APC chairman also raised concerns about alleged threats and conduct by some opposition figures, calling on security agencies to ensure that all political actors operate within the law. Responding on behalf of Governor Abdullahi Sule, the Deputy Governor, Dr Emmanuel Akabe, described the reported incidents as a matter of concern and criticised the security arrangements surrounding the disruption of the Vice-President’s rally. Akabe said security agencies had been briefed ahead of Shettima’s visit and stressed that protecting lives and property remained their responsibility. “It is unfortunate because the responsibility of security men is to protect lives and property. If you cannot protect individuals in your state, then a lot needs to be answered,” he said. The deputy governor disclosed that the State Emergency Security Council had convened to consider measures to prevent further disturbances. He assured the protesters that the state government would support efforts to ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. Speaking on behalf of the Nasarawa State Police Command, Assistant Commissioner of Police Gaya Ahmed reaffirmed the neutrality of security agencies and their commitment to investigating complaints. “The IGP has made it clear that the police are neutral, and we keep on maintaining that neutrality,” Ahmed said. He assured the protesters that petitions submitted by the APC would be forwarded to the incoming Commissioner of Police for investigation. A representative of the Department of State Services (DSS), the Deputy Director of Administration, also acknowledged receipt of the party’s complaints and commended the protesters for conducting themselves peacefully without obstructing public roads. However, the Nasarawa State chapter of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) criticised the demonstration, accusing the state government and the APC of using the protest to target opposition figures. item.title: Court dismisses Maihaja’s suit against Wali’s APC ticket
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu A Federal High Court sitting in Damaturu, Yobe State, has dismissed a suit challenging the emergence of Alhaji Baba Malam Wali as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 general election. The suit was instituted by Engr. Mustapha Yunusa Maihaja, an aspirant in the party’s May 21 governorship primary, who alleged irregularities and non-compliance with the APC’s electoral guidelines. In a judgment delivered on Monday, November 9, 2026, Justice Fatima Murtala Amin held that the suit was statute-barred, having been filed outside the legally prescribed timeframe. The court also found that Maihaja failed to establish his allegations, particularly the claim of over-voting during the governorship primary. Justice Amin upheld a preliminary objection challenging the competence of the suit, thereby dismissing the case on procedural grounds. On the substantive issues, the judge identified material contradictions and inconsistencies in the testimonies of the plaintiff’s witnesses, describing the evidence as unreliable and insufficient to support the allegations. The court further held that even if the suit had been filed within the prescribed timeframe, it would still have failed on its merits because the plaintiff did not provide credible evidence to establish the alleged over-voting. Wali emerged winner of the APC governorship primary with 236,711 votes, securing the party’s ticket for the 2027 governorship election in the state. Reacting to the judgment, Wali’s Press Secretary, Shuaibu Abdullahi, commended the court for its consideration of the issues raised in the suit. “We commend the Court for its painstaking consideration of the issues and reaffirm our confidence in the judiciary as the ultimate guardian of justice and the rule of law,” Abdullahi said. The judgment dismisses the legal challenge to Wali’s emergence as the APC governorship candidate, leaving his party ticket intact ahead of the 2027 general election. item.title: Offa robbery: Saraki faults Kwara govt over amended charges
item.description: Former Senate President, Bukola Saraki, has criticised the Kwara State Government over its decision to amend the criminal charges filed against him and former Governor Abdulfatah Ahmed in connection with the 2018 Offa bank robbery. Saraki described the development as an abuse of the judicial process, questioning the basis for the government’s decision to drop 18 of the original 20 counts and proceed with an amended four-count charge. In a statement issued on Monday by his media aide, Yusuph Olaniyonu, the former Senate President accused the administration of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of pursuing the case for political reasons. The Kwara State Government had, in an application filed on Monday before the state High Court in Ilorin, sought permission to proceed with an amended four-count charge against Saraki, Ahmed and two other defendants. The amended charge, dated November 6, 2026, retains two allegations bordering on conspiracy to belong to a gang of thieves and belonging to a gang of thieves. It also introduces two additional counts relating to the alleged concealment of a Lexus RX Jeep bearing the inscription ‘SARAKI’ as its plate number. Reacting, Saraki said the government had abandoned 18 charges relating to armed robbery after allegedly failing to establish a case against him and Ahmed. He said the government had, since April 2026, been pursuing their arraignment at the State High Court and the Court of Appeal without success. “Last weekend, the state government that has set its legal team to be shuttling between the State High Court and the Court of Appeal seeking without success since April 2026 to arraign the two predecessors of Mr Abdulrazaq on charges of armed robbery suddenly made a U-turn and dropped all 18 charges relating to armed robbery on the Offa case,” the statement said. Saraki alleged that the decision to amend the charges followed the government’s inability to substantiate the allegations against the two former governors. “For fear of failure, the government has chosen to change gear and explore yet other baseless charges,” he said. He described the amendment as evidence, in his view, that the allegations against him and Ahmed lacked a credible factual foundation. “The amendment to the charge sheet only reveals that there was no case against these gentlemen from the beginning and what the state government is indulging in is abuse of powers, a travesty of the justice system, and mockery of the prosecutorial powers of the state,” he added. The former Senate President also questioned the government’s decision to discontinue the 18 counts after allegedly spending close to N100 million publicising its claims against the defendants in national newspapers earlier in the year. He argued that the money could have been channelled into public projects rather than prosecuting allegations he described as unfounded. item.title: [VIDEO] INEC Removes 1,608,660 Invalid Registrants From Voter Register
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has removed 1,608, 660 invalid registrants from the voter register. The Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, who disclosed this at a press briefing on Monday, said the decision was part of an ongoing clean-up exercise, following claims, objections and complaints that trailed the preliminary voter register that was displayed by the commission in October. The clean-up exercise, he explained, also led to the removal from the register of a total of 876 voters, who have been verified as deceased. Amupitan said it would publish the cleaned-up voter register on December 16, 2026, as required by the electoral law.
